This assumption could lead to incorrect behavior if `FLOAT_ARRAY_RANDOM_FUNC` changes in the future without ensuring normalization. The implementation relies on an implicit assumption about the behavior of `FLOAT_ARRAY_RANDOM_FUNC`, introducing a risk that changes to `FLOAT_ARRAY_RANDOM_FUNC` could lead to non-normalized vectors, causing incorrect test results and potentially undetected bugs in vector scoring mechanisms.

review_comment: randomFloat() returns values in the range 0.0f - 1.0f, so will not overflow the arithmetic when passed to `ScalarQuantizedVectorScorer::quantizeQuery` - which will do the normalisation.
Ok yes! I didn't notice it was using the scorer quantization, I thought it was calling scalar quantizer directly.
